content:
Today is day ten of Inkhaven, and this is my tenth substantive post in as many days.

It was easy to publish every day as a member of the first Inkhaven cohort last November. I came to Berkeley with a list of blog post ideas, many fun and quick to write, and I was content to publish stuff that was mediocre on half the days. My job at the time was flexible and fairly chill too, and it was not too difficult for me to reduce my hours for the month.

I don't really identify as a writer, or, if I do, it comes second to my identity as a community organizer. It was difficult for me to agree to return to Inkhaven (having been invited to become an advisor), because it's hard for me to be away from my city and my meetups for long. I miss them, and I feel an acute dereliction of duty, and I feel guilt that I am neglecting the most important thing.

The only way that it could be okay, I thought, was if I fully took advantage of the month. If I did the challenge again, and wrung out all the words that had accumulated inside me. And so I began the challenge at the same time as the third cohort.

This time around, however, a few things are different.

My day job has greater demands of me. Not only do I have a direct report now, much is happening in the policy area that we are focused on, and there is a greater opportunity cost in not getting out the one-pagers and research analyses and proposed bill wordings expeditiously.

I am an advisor, which means I need to dedicate many hours each week to reading the work of the cohort, giving feedback, and designing and running writing-related programming.

As an advisor, I feel immense pressure to only publish works that are good, and not any works that are mediocre. I want to prove that I am a better writer than the residents, so that it makes sense for them to use me as a resource, instead of me being just a weird alum with extra privileges hanging around.

Ben had also made it clear to me how much he would appreciate my full commitment to writing during the month, so that we can help each other grow stronger as writers, and it could be a meaningful experience for us to share as a couple. The NRE is still pretty strong here, such that I really didn't like the idea of disappointing him.

Lastly, I have more drafts that I think are important for me to write with care (rather more care than I think is realistic for a daily publishing program), and not a lot of blog ideas that I think are "easy". Even the "easy" posts — such as Dressing for the Weather, or the Patrick Collison Takedown Post, ended up taking up more time than I thought. I somehow thought that I could knock out the takedown post in three hours, and it ended up taking me the greater part of two days. I had to clean up a draft I would have appreciated more time to consider the implications of and hurriedly publish it in the last few hours of Wednesday night, and this also left me almost no hours for doing my actual job.

I endorse all of these pressures. Still, this has had the unfortunate consequence of me not loving the writing process as much as it deserves to and should be loved. I want to write insofar as it nurtures my writing in all ways — not just the skill of it, but that it makes me feel positively towards the act of writing, and that it resolves dangling questions I have and makes me less confused about the world.

I have decided, therefore, to go on a publishing hiatus for the next ten days, and resume daily publishing for the final third of Inkhaven.

What will I do during my hiatus?

I will still be writing a lot, because there is much I want to write about this month. But without a daily deadline, I will be able to take greater risks in my writing, and cutting.

I will attend many more of the events that are put on by people in this cohort, and get to know the people in it better. I will visit friends in the area, and make new ones. I will make art — more stickers, and I'd like to do a Big Art Project with the cohort too, which might require figuring out the laser printer. I will spend a lot of time with Ben.

And maybe I will still publish a piece or two, if it makes sense to. But if not, I will see you on December 1st.
